title: Reading Drill — Testing screen brightness at an exhibition — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Testing screen brightness at an exhibition — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The exhibition technician had been asked to investigate labels becoming difficult to read beside large windows in Millcross. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the proportion of labels read correctly, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a four-week comparison, the team used short visitor trials at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because clouds changing rapidly might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a matt screen cover. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
